stem:
Ojas pours a small splash of lemon juice into a large glass of water and stirs until the liquid looks even. He also recalls that air is mostly nitrogen with smaller amounts of oxygen and other gases.

Which claims name the solute and the solvent correctly? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: In the lemonade mix, lemon juice is the solute and water is the solvent.
In air, nitrogen is the solvent because it is present in the largest amount.
In the lemonade mix, water is the solute because it is the liquid everyone notices first.
Lemon juice stops being the solute once it can no longer be seen as a separate layer.

teacher.key_rationale: In a liquid-liquid solution the smaller amount is the solute and the larger is the solvent. In air, nitrogen is the solvent as the major component. Visibility or which liquid looks familiar does not rename solute and solvent.
